Question: Consider those functions \(f\) that satisfy \(f(x+4)+f(x-4)=f(x)\) for all real \(x.\) Any such function is periodic, and there is a least common positive period \(p\) for all of them. Find \(p.\)
Solution:
The equation relates inputs spaced 4 apart, so shifting the input by 4 lets us reuse the same relation. Applying it at \(x+4\) and then at \(x+8\) gives
\[
f(x+8)=f(x+4)-f(x)
\]
and
\[
f(x+12)=f(x+8)-f(x+4)=-f(x).
\]
This last identity holds for every real \(x\). Applying it again yields
\[
f(x+24)=-f(x+12)=f(x).
\]
Thus 24 is a period of every allowed function.

To prove that it is the least common positive period, we need one allowed function with no smaller positive period. Define \(g(x)=0\) whenever \(x\) is not a multiple of 4. At multiples of 4, repeat the six-term pattern
\[
1,\ 3,\ 2,\ -1,\ -3,\ -2
\]
in both directions, starting with \(g(0)=1\).

The rule “next value equals current value minus previous value” produces
\[
1,3,2,-1,-3,-2,1,3,
\]
so the repeating pattern satisfies the required equation, including where one repetition joins the next. At inputs that are not multiples of 4, the input and both shifted inputs all have value zero. Therefore \(g\) satisfies the equation for every real input.

The value 1 occurs exactly at inputs \(24k\), where \(k\) is an integer. If \(q>0\) were a period of \(g\), then
\[
g(q)=g(0)=1,
\]
forcing \(q\) to be a positive integer multiple of 24. Hence no smaller positive period works for all the functions. Therefore \(\boxed{p=24}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
